    // True when edge e was accepted: all four of its vertices carry its own number.
    IsAcceptedFlip(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, claims: Array<Integer>, e: Integer): Boolean
    {
        var pair = topology.UndirectedEdges[e];
        var near = self.EdgeApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var far = self.EdgeFarApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        return far.IsPresent
            .And(claims[pair.A.Value] == e)
            .And(claims[pair.B.Value] == e)
            .And(claims[near.Value] == e)
            .And(ClaimAt(claims, far) == e);
    }

    // True when one of the two triangles of edge e is face f.
    FlipTouchesFace(topology: TriangleMeshTopology, e: Integer, f: Integer): Boolean
        => (topology.EdgeCorners[e].Value / 3 == f)
            .Or(topology.CornerTwins[topology.EdgeCorners[e].Value].Value / 3 == f);

    // The accepted flip that rewrites face f, or -1 when the face is untouched.
    FlipOfFace(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, claims: Array<Integer>, f: Integer): Integer
        => topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => e).Reduce(-1, (found, e) =>
            self.IsAcceptedFlip(topology, claims, e).And(FlipTouchesFace(topology, e, f))
                ? e
                : found);

    // The replacement for one of the two triangles of an accepted flip. With the
    // edge running u to v, w the near apex and x the far apex, the quadrilateral
    // reads v, w, u, x counter-clockwise and the new diagonal is w-x; the near
    // triangle becomes (w, u, x) and the far one (w, x, v).
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals.
    FlippedTriangle(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, e: Integer, face: Integer): TriangleFace
    {
        var corner = topology.EdgeCorners[e];
        var twin = topology.CornerTwins[corner.Value];
        var u = self.CornerVertex(corner);
        var v = self.CornerVertex(twin);
        var w = self.CornerVertex(PreviousCorner(corner));
        var x = self.CornerVertex(PreviousCorner(twin));
        return corner.Value / 3 == face ? TriangleFace(w, u, x) : TriangleFace(w, x, v);
    }

    // The face as it stands after the pass: rewritten if a flip claimed it,
    // unchanged otherwise.
    FlippedFaceAt(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, claims: Array<Integer>, face: Integer): TriangleFace
    {
        var e = self.FlipOfFace(topology, claims, face);
        return e < 0 ? self.Faces[face] : self.FlippedTriangle(topology, e, face);
    }

    // Every masked edge flipped at once, subject to the legality and conflict
    // rules above. Positions are untouched and the face count is unchanged.
    FlipEdges(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, flipMask: Array<Boolean>): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var claims = self.FlipVertexClaims(topology, flipMask);
        return (self.Positions,
                self.Faces.Count.MapRange(f => self.FlippedFaceAt(topology, claims, f)));
    }

    // One interior edge flipped. The single-operator form of `FlipEdges`.
    FlipEdge(self: TriangleMesh3D, edge: UndirectedEdgeIndex): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        return self.FlipEdges(topology, SingleEdgeMask(topology.EdgeCount, edge));
    }

    // How far a valence is from the six an interior vertex of a regular
    // triangulation has.
    ValenceDeviation(valence: Integer): Integer
        => (valence - 6).Abs;

    // The valence of a vertex, reading the "none" index as the regular six. A
    // boundary edge has no far apex, and the caller rejects such an edge anyway —
    // this only keeps the arithmetic below off a -1 subscript, because `And` is an
    // ordinary function and therefore does not short-circuit.
    ValenceOrRegular(valences: Array<Integer>, vertex: VertexIndex): Integer
        => vertex.IsNone ? 6 : valences[vertex.Value];

    // True when flipping this edge lowers the total valence deviation of the four
    // vertices involved: the two endpoints each lose a neighbour and the two
    // apexes each gain one. Boundary-touching edges are left alone, because the
    // target valence of a boundary vertex is four rather than six.
    ImprovesValence(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, valences: Array<Integer>,
                    boundary: Array<Boolean>, e: Integer): Boolean
    {
        var pair = topology.UndirectedEdges[e];
        var near = self.EdgeApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var far = self.EdgeFarApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var a = valences[pair.A.Value];
        var b = valences[pair.B.Value];
        var w = ValenceOrRegular(valences, near);
        var x = ValenceOrRegular(valences, far);
        var touchesBoundary = boundary[pair.A.Value].Or(boundary[pair.B.Value])
            .Or(far.IsNone).Or(boundary[near.Value]);
        var before = ValenceDeviation(a) + ValenceDeviation(b)
            + ValenceDeviation(w) + ValenceDeviation(x);
        var after = ValenceDeviation(a - 1) + ValenceDeviation(b - 1)
            + ValenceDeviation(w + 1) + ValenceDeviation(x + 1);
        return touchesBoundary.Not.And(after < before);
    }

    // Every interior edge whose flip brings the triangulation closer to valence
    // six, flipped at once. The regularizing step of isotropic remeshing.
    FlipTowardValenceSix(self: TriangleMesh3D): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        var valences = self.VertexValences(topology);
        var boundary = self.BoundaryVertexFlags(topology);
        return self.FlipEdges(topology, topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e =>
            self.ImprovesValence(topology, valences, boundary, e)));
    }

    //==
    // # Loop and Butterfly subdivision
    //
    // Both refine every triangle into four, so both take their TOPOLOGY from
    // `SplitEdges` with every edge masked and differ only in where the new and old
    // vertices land. Because that function appends the new vertices in edge order
    // after the old ones, a scheme's whole geometric content is one position array
    // laid out the same way: the refined old vertices, then one point per edge.
    //
    // Loop (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_subdivision_surface) is
    // APPROXIMATING — old vertices move, and the limit surface is C2 away from
    // extraordinary vertices. Butterfly
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdivision_surface) is INTERPOLATING — old
    // vertices stay exactly where they are, so the control mesh is on the surface.

    // The mask that selects every edge: the uniform refinement decision.
    AllEdgesMask(topology: TriangleMeshTopology): Array<Boolean>
        => topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => true);

    // Loop's weight for each neighbour of an interior vertex of the given valence
    // (Loop's own choice, as refined by Warren): beta = (5/8 - (3/8 + cos(2 pi / n)
    // / 4)^2) / n.
    LoopBeta(valence: Integer): Number
    {
        var t = 0.375 + (1.0 / valence.ToNumber).Turns.Cos * 0.25;
        return (0.625 - t * t) / valence.ToNumber;
    }

    // Where an old vertex moves under Loop. An interior vertex of valence n keeps
    // 1 - n*beta of itself and spreads beta over each neighbour; a boundary vertex
    // takes the 3/4, 1/8, 1/8 rule over its two boundary neighbours, which keeps
    // the border a cubic B-spline of itself. A vertex with fewer than three
    // neighbours has no rule and stays put.
    LoopVertexPoint(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, neighbors: Array<Array<VertexIndex>>,
                    boundary: Array<Boolean>, v: Integer): Point3D
    {
        var p = self.Positions[v];
        var ring = neighbors[v];
        var beta = LoopBeta(ring.Count);
        var interior = p.PositionVector * (1.0 - ring.Count.ToNumber * beta)
            + ring.Map(n => self.Positions[n.Value]).AverageOfPoints.PositionVector
                * (ring.Count.ToNumber * beta);
        var edge = self.BoundaryNeighborSum(topology, boundary, v);
        return ring.Count < 3 ? p
            : (boundary[v] ? (p.PositionVector * 0.75 + edge * 0.125).ToPoint : interior.ToPoint);
    }
